leads.title: Hezekiah's prayer, Isaiah's oracle against Sennacherib and the angel's slaughter ↔ The companions of the elephant
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God defends the city for his own sake and for the sake of David his servant [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); God defends the city for his own sake and for the sake of David his servant (weight 7.1). Pair score 14.8.

Only in Hezekiah's prayer, Isaiah's oracle against Sennacherib and the angel's slaughter: The angel of YHWH strikes 185,000 in the enemy camp in one night; at dawn all are corpses; The arrogant king boasts of climbing the heights of Lebanon and cutting its cedars, drying up rivers with his feet; Proverb of crisis: children have come to the birth-stool and there is no strength to deliver; When the punishment descends in their courtyard, evil will be the morning of those who were warned; God says the conqueror's victories were planned by him long ago; the conqueror is only his instrument; The king tears his clothes, puts on sackcloth and goes into the temple in crisis; Royal parricides flee to the land of Ararat; The escaped remnant shall again take root downward and bear fruit upward; a remnant goes out from Zion; God puts a spirit in the invader so that he hears a rumor and returns home; King spreads the enemy's threatening letter before God in the temple; Sign: this year eat aftergrowth, next year what springs of itself, the third year sow and reap; The 'virgin daughter of Zion' laughs at and wags her head after the enemy; and 8 more.

Only in The companions of the elephant: God sends birds in flocks (tayran ababil) that pelt an army with stones of baked clay (sijjil), leaving them like devoured straw; God's action against the companions of the elephant (ashab al-fil), whose plot he made go astray; The angel of YHWH strikes 185,000 in the enemy camp in one night; at dawn all are corpses [divergence between the texts]; God casts great hailstones from heaven, killing more than the sword; The wicked are like chaff driven by the wind.
